Downstream consumers in `src/commands/worktree/switch.rs` (`fetch_same_repo_branch`, `resolve_switch_target`) assume `RemoteRefInfo.source_branch` is non-empty and construct invalid git refspecs (`+refs/heads/:refs/remotes/<remote>/`) and worktree paths.
trigger: Running `wt switch pr:<N>` against an Azure DevOps PR whose API response has `sourceRefName` equal to `""` or `"refs/heads/"`.
match_rule: Identify that `azure.rs::fetch_pr_info` does not reject an empty `source_branch` after stripping `refs/heads/` (unlike sibling `github.rs` and `gitlab.rs` providers), letting an empty branch name propagate into `RemoteRefInfo` and downstream `switch.rs` git refspec/worktree operations.
near_misses: Complaining about `parse_web_url` org/project parsing or `*.visualstudio.com` host handling in `azure.rs` without identifying the missing empty `source_branch` validation at the provider boundary.
why_findable: Both sibling providers `src/git/remote_ref/github.rs:193` (`if response.head.ref_name.is_empty()`) and `src/git/remote_ref/gitlab.rs:139` (`if response.source_branch.is_empty()`) validate non-empty `source_branch` before constructing `RemoteRefInfo`, while `azure.rs` lines 262-266 strip `refs/heads/` and pass `source_branch` straight into `RemoteRefInfo`.
notes: Fix commit f68626dd adds the empty `source_branch` check in `azure.rs::fetch_pr_info` and adds `test_switch_pr_azure_empty_source_branch`.

defect: In copy_dir_recursive_fallback, symlink preservation guards symlink creation with `if !dest_path.exists()`. Because Path::exists() follows symlinks, it returns false for a broken (dangling) symlink already present at dest_path, causing a repeated `wt step copy-ignored` run to attempt symlink creation again and fail with AlreadyExists (EEXIST) instead of skipping it idempotently.
trigger: Run `wt step copy-ignored` twice when an ignored directory contains a broken symlink whose target does not exist; on the second run `dest_path.exists()` returns false for the existing broken symlink and `symlink(&target, &dest_path)` fails with EEXIST.
match_rule: Identifies that `dest_path.exists()` in `copy_dir_recursive_fallback` follows symlinks and returns false for dangling/broken symlinks, so re-running `copy-ignored` fails with AlreadyExists instead of using `symlink_metadata()` or handling `ErrorKind::AlreadyExists`.
near_misses: Complaining about symlink traversal security or Windows symlink_dir detection without identifying that `dest_path.exists()` misses broken symlinks on repeated runs.
why_findable: Directly visible in `copy_dir_recursive_fallback` at `d97c0e99`: regular files right below handle `ErrorKind::AlreadyExists` for idempotent hook usage, while the newly added symlink branch guards creation with `!dest_path.exists()` instead of `symlink_metadata().is_err()` or catching `AlreadyExists`.
notes: d97c0e99 introduced symlink copying in copy_dir_recursive_fallback (previously symlinks were skipped); local control (relation=false) because the entire bug is inside copy_dir_recursive_fallback. Brings copy-ignored feature spread to 2 (with [4] a0f46175).

defect: execute_streaming unconditionally sets `.stdin(std::process::Stdio::null())` on the spawned child command. While intended for non-interactive hooks, InteractiveOutput::execute calls execute_streaming to run `wt switch --execute <cmd>`, starving interactive `--execute` programs (such as editors, REPLs, or `cat`) of stdin with immediate EOF.
trigger: Run `wt switch <branch> --execute <interactive-cmd>` (e.g., piping input to `wt switch --create stdin-test --execute cat` or launching `vim`/`claude`) in interactive output mode; the executed command receives immediate EOF on stdin.
match_rule: Connects the unconditional `.stdin(Stdio::null())` added to `execute_streaming` in `src/output/handlers.rs` with its interactive caller `InteractiveOutput::execute` in `src/output/interactive.rs`, identifying that `--execute` commands lose stdin inheritance and receive immediate EOF.
near_misses: Flagging only that hooks cannot read stdin (hooks are intentionally non-interactive) without linking to `InteractiveOutput::execute` / `wt switch --execute`.
why_findable: Looking at all callers of `execute_streaming` at `6e0d040f` immediately shows `InteractiveOutput::execute` uses it for `wt switch --execute` (explicitly passing `redirect_stdout_to_stderr = false` for interactive execution), which requires inherited stdin.
notes: At 6e0d040f, InteractiveOutput::execute called execute_streaming on all platforms (Unix later switched to exec(), leaving Windows broken until bc05b5e0). Before 6e0d040f, execute_streaming inherited stdin by default.

defect: handle_merge pushes `ApprovableCommand::commit_template_append(...)` into the same `all_commands` batch as merge hooks, passes the combined list to `approve_command_batch` (which filters out already-approved commands and returns a single bool), and uses that single `approved` bool to set `commit_hooks = HookGate::from_approval(verify, approved)` and shadow `verify = false`. When project hooks are already approved and only `commit.generation.template-append` is prompted, declining the commit-message append returns `false` and silently disables all already-approved merge hooks.
trigger: Configure an LLM commit generator, already-approved project hooks (e.g., pre-merge/post-merge), and an unapproved project `[commit.generation] template-append`, then run `wt merge` and decline the prompt; the already-approved hooks are skipped instead of running.

near_misses: Complaining generally about UI prompt grouping without identifying that `approve_command_batch` filters out already-approved commands and returns one boolean that flips `verify` to false and suppresses already-approved hooks.
why_findable: Cross-checking `handle_merge` against `approve_command_batch` shows `approve_command_batch` strips already-approved items before prompting and returns `Ok(false)` when the remaining unapproved item (the commit template append) is declined, which `handle_merge` then applies to `verify` and `commit_hooks` for the entire merge.
notes: f522357e introduced project-level commit.generation.template-append and bundled it into handle_merge's hook approval batch. Neither commit message nor comments flag the skip-approved-hooks bug.

defect: Repository::primary_remote runs `git config --get-regexp r"remote\..+\.url"` without anchoring the pattern with `^` and only inspects `output.lines().next()` with `line.strip_prefix("remote.")`. Any non-remote config key containing `remote.<x>.url` (such as `includeIf.hasconfig:remote.*.url:...`) matches first, fails `strip_prefix("remote.")`, and causes `primary_remote()` to return None/fallback "origin" instead of finding the configured remote.
trigger: In a repo with a non-origin remote (e.g., `upstream`) and a git config key like `includeIf.hasconfig:remote.*.url:...` appearing earlier in `git config --get-regexp` output, call `Repository::primary_remote()`; it takes only the first matching line, `strip_prefix("remote.")` yields None, and it falls back to "origin".
match_rule: Identifies that `r"remote\..+\.url"` passed to `git config --get-regexp` is unanchored (missing `^`) and/or that `output.lines().next()` aborts on the first non-`remote.` matching line (such as `includeIf.hasconfig:remote.*.url`) instead of anchoring or using `find_map`.
near_misses: Complaining about remote names containing spaces or `.url` substrings inside the URL value without noting the unanchored regex + `.lines().next()` failure on non-`remote.` config keys.
why_findable: Directly visible in the 10-line fallback block added by `cfde3ffe`: `git config --get-regexp` matches anywhere in the key unless anchored with `^`, yet the parser immediately calls `.lines().next()` and `strip_prefix("remote.")`.
notes: cfde3ffe replaced `git remote` with `git config --get-regexp r"remote\..+\.url"` + `.lines().next()`. Local control (relation=false) because the entire bug is inside Repository::primary_remote.

defect: Global `-C <path>` in `main.rs` only sets `Repository`'s base path via `apply_global_options` -> `set_base_path` (not the process cwd) and passes `working_dir` into `dispatch_command` so commands that spawn child processes directly (like `Commands::Custom`) can apply `.current_dir()`. `408f4f5b` wired `StepCommand::Tether` into `handle_step_command(action, yes)` without passing `working_dir`, and `step_tether` spawns `std::process::Command::new(&command[0])` directly without ever calling `Repository::current()` or setting `.current_dir()`, so `wt -C <dir> step tether -- <cmd>` (despite advertising `-C <path>` as a Global Option in `wt step tether --help`) silently ignores `-C` and runs the command in the caller's cwd.
trigger: Run `wt -C <subdir> step tether -- <cmd>` from a parent directory; `<cmd>` executes with cwd equal to the parent directory instead of `<subdir>`.
match_rule: Connects how global `-C <path>` is implemented in `src/main.rs` (`set_base_path` for `Repository` plus `working_dir` passed in `dispatch_command` only to `Commands::Custom`, not `Commands::Step`) with `step_tether` in `src/commands/step/tether.rs` spawning `std::process::Command` directly without `.current_dir()` or `Repository::current()`, causing `wt -C <dir> step tether` to silently ignore `-C`.
near_misses: Commenting only on whether the reaper should watch `-C` vs cwd without noticing that the spawned tethered command never receives `-C` as its working directory at all.
why_findable: Comparing the new `StepCommand::Tether` dispatch path in `src/main.rs` against `dispatch_command` (which explicitly threads `working_dir` to `Commands::Custom` because `set_base_path` does not chdir the process) and `step_tether` (which never touches `Repository` or `base_path`) directly reveals that global `-C` is silently dropped for `wt step tether`.
notes: 408f4f5b introduced `wt step tether` and its generated help docs explicitly list `-C <path>: Working directory for this command`, while dispatch_command already carried `working_dir` for non-Repository subprocess commands (`Commands::Custom`).

defect: 73b4f8305 switched `step_for_each` from `run_command_streaming` (which did not trap signals in `wt`, so Ctrl-C terminated `wt` and aborted the loop) to `execute_shell_command`, which runs `Cmd::shell(...).forward_signals().stream()`. On Unix, `.forward_signals()` installs `Signals::new([SIGINT, SIGTERM])` in the parent `wt` process, forwards the signal to the child's process group, and returns `Err(WorktrunkError::ChildProcessExited { code: 128 + sig, message })` without killing `wt`. `step_for_each` catches every `Err` from `execute_shell_command`, logs it as a per-worktree failure, and continues launching the command in all remaining worktrees (and exits 1 instead of 128 + sig).
trigger: Run `wt step for-each -- <cmd>` across multiple worktrees and interrupt with Ctrl-C (`SIGINT`) or `SIGTERM` (or run a child that dies from a signal like `kill -TERM $$`); `wt` traps/converts the signal into `ChildProcessExited` instead of aborting, keeps iterating through remaining worktrees, and exits with code 1 instead of 128 + signal.
match_rule: Connects `step_for_each` in `src/commands/for_each.rs` catching all `Err(ChildProcessExited)` and continuing the worktree loop with `execute_shell_command` (`src/output/handlers.rs`) enabling `.forward_signals()` -> `Cmd::stream()` (`src/shell_exec.rs`) trapping `SIGINT`/`SIGTERM` in `wt` and returning `ChildProcessExited { code: 128 + sig }` without distinguishing signal termination, causing Ctrl-C/signal exits to continue looping instead of aborting.
near_misses: Complaining only that `for-each` continues on ordinary non-zero exit codes (intentional behavior) without identifying signal forwarding / `SIGINT`/`SIGTERM` trapping returning `ChildProcessExited` into the catch-and-continue loop.
why_findable: Following `step_for_each` -> `execute_shell_command` -> `Cmd::stream` at `73b4f8305` shows `for-each` newly gained `.forward_signals()`, which traps `SIGINT`/`SIGTERM` in the parent `wt` process and converts them to `Err(WorktrunkError::ChildProcessExited { code: 128 + sig })` that `step_for_each` unconditionally catches and continues past.
notes: At 73b4f8305^, run_command_streaming did not trap SIGINT/SIGTERM in wt, so Ctrl-C terminated wt immediately and aborted the loop; 73b4f8305 added .forward_signals() to for-each. test_for_each_aborts_on_signal_exit drives the ChildProcessExited signal path via in-child `kill -TERM $$` and deterministically fails at 00c41895f2^ (exits 1 without 'Interrupted' instead of 143).

defect: In `handle_removed_worktree_output`, `22698cf18` inserted `execute_pre_remove_commands(&ctx, false)?` (lines 491-504) after `super::change_directory(main_path)?; super::flush()?;` (lines 458-461). why_findable: Directly visible inside `handle_removed_worktree_output` at `22698cf18`: lines 457-461 emit and flush the `cd` directive ('shell will execute this immediately'), and lines 491-504 run `execute_pre_remove_commands` ('Non-zero exit aborts removal') afterwards.

Local control (relation=false) because the ordering bug is fully visible within handle_removed_worktree_output. test_pre_remove_hook_failure_no_cd_directive deterministically fails at 6b6751ec06^ because the directive file contains `cd `.
